entities.name: United States
entities.summary: Home jurisdiction of most frontier AI labs, the dominant chipmaker, and the primary AI capital markets.

entities.name: China
entities.summary: Home jurisdiction of the leading open-weight AI labs and the other pole of the US-China AI capability race.

entities.name: France
entities.summary: Home jurisdiction of Mistral AI and the EU's self-styled sovereign-AI champion.

entities.name: United Kingdom
entities.summary: Home jurisdiction of the AI Security Institute and Apollo Research, active in frontier-model evaluation.

entities.name: Taiwan
entities.summary: Home jurisdiction of TSMC, the sole leading-edge foundry for nearly all frontier AI chips.

entities.name: Japan
entities.summary: Home jurisdiction of SoftBank Group, a major capital and compute-infrastructure partner to US frontier labs.

entities.name: Canada
entities.summary: Home jurisdiction of Mila, a leading academic deep-learning research institute.

entities.name: Australia
entities.summary: Member jurisdiction of the International AI Safety Institute Network.

entities.name: Singapore
entities.summary: Member jurisdiction of the International AI Safety Institute Network.

entities.name: South Korea
entities.summary: Member jurisdiction of the International AI Safety Institute Network and an AI summit host.

entities.name: India
entities.summary: Host of the 2026 AI Action Summit in the Bletchley/Seoul/Paris summit series.

entities.name: United Arab Emirates
entities.summary: Home jurisdiction of sovereign wealth vehicles MGX and Mubadala that co-anchor frontier-lab funding rounds.

entities.name: Saudi Arabia
entities.summary: Home jurisdiction of the Public Investment Fund, a sovereign backer of frontier AI compute deals.

entities.name: National Institute of Standards and Technology
entities.summary: US Commerce Department standards agency that now hosts CAISI, the government's frontier-model testing body.

entities.name: Center for AI Standards and Innovation
entities.summary: US government body housed in NIST that tests frontier AI models, renamed in mid-2025 from the U.S. AI Safety Institute.

entities.name: UK AI Security Institute
entities.summary: UK government body evaluating frontier models for national-security risk, renamed from the AI Safety Institute in February 2025.

entities.name: European AI Office
entities.summary: European Commission body that develops guidance for and enforces the EU AI Act's general-purpose-AI obligations.

entities.name: Cyberspace Administration of China
entities.summary: China's internet and AI regulator, responsible for generative-AI service approvals that Chinese labs must clear before public release.

entities.name: U.S. Federal Trade Commission
entities.summary: Primary US enforcement agency for AI-related consumer-protection and competition actions against large tech platforms.

entities.name: International AI Safety Institute Network
entities.summary: Coalition of national AI safety/security institutes launched from the Bletchley Summit process to coordinate frontier-model evaluation.

entities.name: OpenAI
entities.summary: Creator of GPT and ChatGPT, a capped-profit company controlled by an affiliated nonprofit foundation.

entities.name: Anthropic
entities.summary: Public benefit corporation and builder of the Claude model family, founded by ex-OpenAI researchers.

entities.name: Alphabet Inc.
entities.summary: Parent holding company of Google and Google DeepMind, and owner of the TPU custom-silicon program.

entities.name: Google DeepMind
entities.summary: Alphabet's unified AI research and product lab, builder of the Gemini model family.

entities.name: xAI
entities.summary: Elon Musk's AI lab and builder of the Grok model family, acquired by SpaceX in February 2026.

entities.name: SpaceX
entities.summary: Elon Musk's aerospace company that acquired xAI in a $1.25 trillion combination in February 2026.

entities.name: Meta Platforms
entities.summary: Parent company whose AI division builds the open-weight Llama models and now houses Meta Superintelligence Labs.

entities.name: Meta Superintelligence Labs
entities.summary: Meta's 2025-restructured AI research and product unit, encompassing FAIR and the frontier-model TBD Lab.

entities.name: Mistral AI
entities.summary: Paris-based frontier lab and Europe's leading open-weight and commercial model builder, positioned as the EU's sovereign-AI champion.

entities.name: Nvidia
entities.summary: Dominant AI accelerator maker and owner of the CUDA software ecosystem that underpins most frontier model training.

entities.name: DeepSeek
entities.summary: Hangzhou-based Chinese lab whose efficient open-weight releases reset assumptions about frontier training cost.

entities.name: Alibaba Group
entities.summary: Chinese conglomerate whose Alibaba Cloud unit builds the widely-adopted open-weight Qwen model family.

entities.name: Moonshot AI
entities.summary: Chinese lab behind the Kimi open-weight model family, competing aggressively on cost and long-context performance.

entities.name: Zhipu AI
entities.summary: Chinese lab behind the GLM model family, rebranded consumer-facing products under the Z.ai name.

entities.name: Baidu
entities.summary: Chinese search giant and builder of the ERNIE model family, a longstanding China-market AI incumbent.

entities.name: Microsoft
entities.summary: OpenAI's largest strategic investor and Azure cloud partner, also shipping its own Copilot product line.

entities.name: Amazon
entities.summary: Major cloud provider and Anthropic investor that builds custom Trainium/Inferentia AI silicon.

entities.name: Apple
entities.summary: Ships on-device and cloud AI as Apple Intelligence, a comparatively slower-moving frontier participant but a major distribution channel via iOS.

entities.name: AMD
entities.summary: Nvidia's primary GPU/accelerator challenger, anchored by a large multi-year OpenAI compute deal.

entities.name: Broadcom
entities.summary: Critical custom-silicon design partner for hyperscaler AI ASICs, including Google's TPUs and OpenAI's in-house accelerator program.

entities.name: TSMC
entities.summary: Sole leading-edge foundry for nearly all frontier AI chips, making its CoWoS packaging capacity an industry-wide constraint.

entities.name: METR
entities.summary: Berkeley-based nonprofit that runs independent capability and dangerous-capability evaluations on frontier models.

entities.name: Epoch AI
entities.summary: Nonprofit research group tracking compute trends, training-run scale, and frontier AI progress data.

entities.name: Apollo Research
entities.summary: AI safety organization specializing in evaluating models for deceptive alignment and scheming behavior.

entities.name: Machine Intelligence Research Institute
entities.summary: The oldest dedicated AI safety research organization, focused on theoretical alignment and existential-risk research.

entities.name: Center for AI Safety
entities.summary: Nonprofit behind the widely signed statement on AI risk and ongoing benchmark and policy advocacy work.

entities.name: Allen Institute for AI
entities.summary: Seattle nonprofit research lab producing fully open models, datasets, and benchmarks such as the OLMo series.

entities.name: Hugging Face
entities.summary: The dominant open model and dataset hosting hub, functioning as the de facto distribution layer for open-weight AI.

entities.name: EleutherAI
entities.summary: Grassroots nonprofit open-research collective known for GPT-J, GPT-NeoX, Pythia, and the Pile dataset.

entities.name: Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI
entities.summary: Academic policy and research hub best known for the annual AI Index Report, a widely cited industry-trends benchmark.

entities.name: Mila – Quebec AI Institute
entities.summary: Montreal-based academic AI research institute associated with Yoshua Bengio, a leading deep-learning research center.

entities.name: Andreessen Horowitz
entities.summary: Leading venture capital firm with a dedicated AI investment strategy and among the most active foundation-model backers.

entities.name: Sequoia Capital
entities.summary: Major venture firm with sustained frontier-model and applied-AI investments alongside sovereign wealth funds.

entities.name: Thrive Capital
entities.summary: Josh Kushner's venture firm and one of OpenAI's most concentrated institutional backers across multiple funding rounds.

entities.name: SoftBank Group
entities.summary: Japanese conglomerate and major OpenAI investor and compute-infrastructure partner behind the Stargate project.

entities.name: MGX
entities.summary: UAE state-backed investment vehicle co-anchoring mega-rounds and compute infrastructure deals for OpenAI and xAI.

entities.name: Public Investment Fund
entities.summary: Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund, an increasingly active co-anchor of frontier AI mega-rounds.

entities.name: Mubadala Investment Company
entities.summary: Abu Dhabi sovereign wealth fund co-anchoring mega-rounds and compute infrastructure deals for frontier AI labs.

entities.name: Microsoft

entities.name: Amazon

entities.name: Apple
entities.summary: Ships on-device and cloud AI as Apple Intelligence, a comparatively slower-moving frontier participant but a major distribution channel via iOS.

entities.name: AMD

entities.name: Broadcom

entities.name: TSMC

entities.name: METR

entities.name: Epoch AI

entities.name: Apollo Research
entities.summary: AI safety organization specializing in evaluating models for deceptive alignment and scheming behavior.

entities.name: Center for AI Safety

entities.name: Sequoia Capital
